steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.

In a medium saucepan, bring the water to a boil. Stir in grits, and reduce heat to low. Cover, and cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally. Mix in the butter, cheese, seasoning salt, Worcestershire sauce, hot pepper sauce, and salt. Continue cooking for 5 minutes, or until the cheese is melted. Remove from heat, cool slightly, and fold in the eggs. Pour into the prepared baking dish.
Bake 1 hour in the preheated oven, or until the top is lightly browned.

raw_recipe.headline: Oklahoma Cheese Grits
raw_recipe.description: It's a great day when my mom serves up this Southern specialty! Cooked grits are combined with seasonings, cheese, and eggs, then baked. You may adjust or eliminate the hot sauce to suit your taste.
raw_recipe.name: Oklahoma Cheese Grits

review.reviewBody: I've made these several times now with a few changes: I use cheddar/Jack cheeses instead of processed, and I double the hot sauce (Tapatio) and omit the seasoning salt; I also leave out the eggs, as they just don't seem necessary. What I want to point out is that this can really be a one-dish meal. It's not necessary to cook everything atop the stove and then transfer to a baking dish for the oven. I simply throw all the ingredients together in a baking dish, then toss it in the oven. After about half an hour, I stir well, then let it go for another half hour or so. The grits are cooked to perfection, and I just made a very easy, quick meal! My family loves it, so on occasion, I throw it together for dinner. The ease of it all makes me happy, and they're happy 'cause they like it so much!

I made these for a breakfast pitchin for work. They were very good. I used 8oz shredded sharp cheddar cheese and 8 slices of processed american cheese. For the salt, I used 2 tsp garlic salt and 1 tsp regular salt. I left out the worcestershire sauce. I baked them in my slow cooker crock, then plugged it in when I got to work to keep them warm. It worked great! I will make these again.

JUST the grits recipe I was looking for! I especially appreciate the suggestions made to simply combine everything in a baking dish, throw it in the oven, stir it up after cooking a half hour and then finishing it in the oven for another 30 min. It came out great! Also I did agree with the changes to cut out the seasoning salt and eggs altogether and cut the butter back to a 1/4 cup....it STILL tasted fantastic! Also I chose to do a mix of 2/3 pepper jack cheese to 1/3 processed cheese. DELISH!

I make this every year at Xmas -- a tradition in this Northern home ! I usually use the Microwave directions for the grits .. and use a large 8 cup pyrex dish. You can mix it all together in the pyrex dish before transferring to baking dish. I always use bagged shredded sharp cheddar instead of processed. And I use garlic salt not seasoned salt. Delicious !

Caveat: Neither I or my better half are grits fans but we loved it. Tweaks we made: We cut the recipe in half for two people. Keeping in mind we cut the recipe in half, we used 1 teaspoon of season salt but replaced the 1 teaspoon of salt with 1 teaspoon of season salt. Next time, I would reduce the 2 teaspoons of season salt to 1.25 or 1.5 teaspoons of season salt and just leave out the salt. We also added 1 cup of diced ham to our "half" batch and used just 2 eggs. Finally, I baked it in an 8x8 pyrex dish in my oven using convection mode at 375 for 50 minutes. On my convection oven reduces the temp approx. 25 degrees... that's why I bumped it up. Finally next time instead of using the 8x8 for the half batch, I will use a 9x13 so the finished product is thinner and hopefully a little firmer.

I make these for every family special occasion. The recipe is great as is, but my family likes a little heat so I typically use the Mexican Velveeta and add a can of chopped green chiles and/or some chopped jalapeños. Toss a handful of grated cheddar or jack in along with the process cheese then sprinkle a little on top for color. They are great with any meat as a side dish but also wonderful for breakfast.

I just made this scaled down to four for my small family in an 8X8 pan using several reviewers' suggestions. I omitted seasoning salt (didn't have it), used cheddar cheese (it's what I had), omitted Worcestershire sauce cause I was making this for breakfast, added some precooked sausage (to use it up), and most importantly, followed Brandy Lee's suggestion to just dump all the ingredients in without precooking the grits. That was a huge time saver. Also, I didn't even realize it when I was eating them that I'd completely forgotten to add the butter! Oops! We didn't miss it at all, so I guess those who want to save calories could leave it out. I might add a little the next time I make them just for curiosity and comparison, but these were great without it.

I'm southern born and raised and I have eaten grits my entire life. Somehow, I have never made proper cheese grits before. Beyond just tossing some cheese into a pot of grits. I was to attend a potluck brunch, so I decided to give these cheese grits a shot. I omitted the hot sauce and added some shredded cheddar to the top but otherwise stayed true to this recipe. Let me tell you, this dish was amazing. Everyone raved over them. Even the non grits people loved it. Needless to say, there were no leftovers. This one is a keeper.

Great recipe! I scaled the serving size down to 6 for just my husband & I and baked in an 8x10 dish for 40 minutes. Perfect! My husband ate almost the entire dish. I would substitute another kind of cheese just b/c I am not a fan of the velveeta cheese, so I think I will cut the amount of cheese in half next time. Thanks!
Addictive! Easy and fabulous. Loved making it in the crockpot as opposed to the oven because I was able to keep it warm all day.

This Yankee FINALLY realized why all the fuss over grits... I used the real thing instead of instant grits. (cooked ratio of 1:3 grits to water for about 15 -20 minutes.) This is the only time I've ever liked grits.
I’ve always mixed my scrambled eggs and grits together, need to crumble your crisp bacon on top. Yum

I enjoy this method of cooking grits. For those saying baking and adding eggs is unnecessary; I recommend you actually try it this way. The result is a much lighter and refined texture. I do usually use chicken broth and often add bacon pieces (cooked in a skillet prior to baking) Definitely try this method, it's worth the effort.
Followed the suggestion to add crumbled breakfast sausage (used the maple style)... great brunch with Michelada cocktails! Thanks for sharing the recipe.

Overall I liked this recipe, a different way of making grits that I have been making and eating all my life. I realized at the last minute I didn’t have worchesire sauce, I had soy sauce so I omitted it completely, I didn’t add the seasoning salt to reduce sodium, I used half the salt and half the butter to reduce cholesterol. Instead of processed cheese I used pepper Jack cheese, shredded Colby Jack, and a little smoked Gouda. I did use the hot sauce and eggs. All the cheeses and hot sauce made it plenty salty enough so didn’t miss the seasonings. Pretty good to me. Ill make it again
Changed it alot. Browned chopped little link breakfast sausages. Cooked it with grits altogether. Combined everything and baked.
This was a big hit at our house. I made it as is and we really enjoyed it.
Boom! Yes! I was sad when it was all gone and I didn't have any leftovers.
Best cheese grits ever!!! Everyone always loves when I make these cheese grits
It was great! I will only limit the salt next time. Keep in mind I LOVE salty foods.
